MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary Various
Remuneration: $117,745 - $147,664
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM29661

Living in our region
We provide a fantastic place to call home; Newcastle and surrounds have a beautiful, relaxed yet active lifestyle for individuals, couples and families alike. We have great hospitals; work within a network of hospitals all interrelated and supportive of each other, our EDs are growing and expanding beyond the realm of just clinical service delivery to teach and support Trainees in undertaking research, ultrasound skills, trauma, education terms, to mention a few. We pride ourselves on a culture of learning and education, role modelling and mentorship with professionalism. We want to grow our Trainees into not only excellent doctors, but excellent people who love our community as much as we do.

Where you will be working
You will be working in our dynamic Emergency Network which include John Hunter Hospital, Maitland Hospital, Belmont Hospital, Calvary Mater Newcastle, Tamworth Rural Referral Hospital, Port Macquarie Base Hospital and Manning Base Hospital. These sites offer fantastic metropolitan and rural experiences in Emergency Medicine and speciality terms for our ACEM Trainees.
John Hunter Hospital is one of the busiest Emergency Departments in Australia with Trauma and Retrieval focused presentations. Should you only require Tertiary time for your Training, this can be facilitated within the Network at John Hunter Hospital.

What you will be doing
The primary purpose of Trainee Stage 2-4 in Emergency Medicine is to provide high-quality medical care under appropriate supervision to undifferentiated patients presenting to the Emergency Department.
Our Emergency Medicine Network sites are fully accredited and meet all requirements for advanced training with the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM). We are proud of our consistently strong Fellowship examination outcomes, supported by a comprehensive education and training program that is closely aligned with the ACEM curriculum and focused on examination success.

Trainees have access to a diverse range of rotations across tertiary and metropolitan adult and paediatric Emergency Departments, as well as placements in intensive care, anaesthetics, retrieval medicine, inpatient and emergency paediatrics, ultrasound, and medical education. Complementing our strong Emergency Medicine training program is our outstanding Simulation Centre, with our FACEMs highly committed to simulation-based education, mentorship, and trainee development.
Trainees work under a level of supervision according to their competence in the following activities; Taking a leadership role in coordinating the admission, assessment, management, and discharge planning of patients. Communicating assessment and management decisions to other staff involved in the patient's care. Communicating with the patient - family regarding the patient's condition and management plans. Coordinating diagnostic tests and consultations with other medical specialists. Arranging the patient discharge process and liaising with local medical officers and community based care modalities for optimal post discharge care.

For more information on working and living in our beautiful Network 4 please follow the below links.

https:--youtu.be-GWdrT5iLn-Yhttps:--www.hnehealth.nsw.gov.au-professionals-medical-training-positions-emergency-medicine-training

https:--www.destinationtamworth.com.au-Home-tamworth-visitor-information-centre

Contracts of up to three years duration are offered.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Qualifications and experience commensurate with the Essential Requirements for the role.

Demonstrated ability to work with appropriate independence, commensurate with a level of a Specialist Trainee, within a supervised complex clinical environment.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively as part of a multi-disciplinary team in the planning, delivery and coordination of patient care.

Demonstrated high level written and verbal communication skills and ability to communicate effectively and respectfully with patients, family members and others members of the health care team.

Demonstrated good organisational and time management skills and ability to manage competing priorities in a complex environment.

Demonstrated commitment to quality improvement, patient safety and risk management.

Evidence of continuing professional development and commitment to self education.

Previous experience in and willingness to deliver undergraduate and postgraduate medical education and training.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary Various
Remuneration: $94,521 - $127,827
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM30445

Why choose the Northern Paediatric Training Network?

Train in Tertiary Paediatrics. Thrive Across Metropolitan, Regional and Rural NSW.
 

Where you'll be working

This position is within the Northern Paediatric Training Network (NPTN) NSW. Our Network comprises a number of hospitals located across metropolitan, regional and rural settings.

Our base hospital is John Hunter Children's Hospital, a tertiary paediatric hospital located in Newcastle, NSW - a vibrant coastal city approximately two hours' drive north of Sydney. John Hunter Children's Hospital provides subspecialty and general multidisciplinary care for children with complex medical and surgical conditions. We are also a major trauma centre and home to the largest Level 4 surgical Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) in NSW.

Our other Network hospitals include Gosford-Wyong Hospitals and The Maitland Hospital.

From the deep blue Pacific Ocean and sandy beaches to lush forest reserves, nature trails, ocean baths, picturesque countryside and renowned wine regions, the Hunter and Central Coast regions offer an exceptional lifestyle with easy access to both city amenities and outdoor recreation.

What you'll be doing

Successful candidates will:

Work alongside a diverse team of medical, nursing and allied health professionals.

Practise effective, evidence-based paediatric medicine under the supervision of experienced senior clinicians.

Further develop clinical skills and competence in a supportive training environment, including but not limited to:

Management of acute and chronic paediatric conditions.

Paediatric and neonatal procedures.

Facilitating multidisciplinary management.

Coordinating diagnostic investigations in consultation with other medical specialists.

Supporting continuity of care in the community following discharge.

Contribute to a friendly, multidisciplinary team environment that reflects our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment.

Responsibilities include

Coordinating the admission, management and discharge planning of patients seen in or admitted to the Children's Ward and Special Care Nursery-Unit, ensuring that assessments, treatment plans and clinical decisions are appropriately documented in the medical record.

Undertaking the day-to-day assessment and management of patients within the allocated clinical unit and communicating effectively with patients and their families regarding their condition, treatment and ongoing care.

Communicating and coordinating care with the multidisciplinary team, arranging consultation with other medical staff when appropriate, facilitating discharge planning, and liaising with local medical officers and community-based care providers.

Contributing to the provision of outpatient paediatric services.

Ensuring that all patient management decisions are made in consultation with the immediate supervisor and within the scope of delegated clinical responsibility.

What we can provide to you

This role offers an outstanding opportunity to:

Experience tertiary paediatric medicine at a leading teaching institution that also hosts the University of Newcastle undergraduate medical programme.

Engage in continuous medical education, teaching and research opportunities.

Work within a roster structure capped at 40 hours per week, with generous leave benefits including 4 weeks annual leave, sick leave and long service leave accruals.

Gain valuable exposure to rural paediatric medicine through rotations across our broader Network.

Enjoy the unique lifestyle of the Hunter and Central Coast regions - surf, sand and big blue skies are all part of the experience.

We are an inclusive community and welcome team members from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, First Nations communities and LGBTQIA+ communities.

Important links for your information

For more information about working and living in the beautiful Hunter New England Local Health District region, please explore the following:

Fun in the Vines
What's great about Newcastle
What's great about the Country life
What's great about the Lake

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

MBBS or equivalent, currently registered or eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia.

Minimum 2 years postgraduate experience.

Demonstrated interest in Paediatric Medicine.

Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams, including the sharing of appropriate information internally and externally with key persons or services.

Demonstrated ability to work independently within a supervised complex clinical environment, utilising excellent clinical skills, judgement and expertise.

A professional attitude and flexibility in work role with a preparedness and ability to participate in after-hours overtime and on-call rosters.

Demonstrated commitment to self-education, continued professional development, teaching, and quality improvement, with a strong focus on patient safety and risk management

WHERE YOU'LL BE AND WHAT YOU'LL DO

Hammill House Residential Aged Care Facility is located in Port Pirie, 223 kilometres north of Adelaide. Known as the City of Opportunity, Port Pirie is a vibrant regional centre offering major retail, tourism, arts, and sporting events. Set between the Southern Flinders Ranges and the Spencer Gulf, the city provides a stunning lifestyle where rolling hills meet beautiful coastline, with easy access to some of the region's most diverse and scenic hiking trails.

Hammill House is a compassionate, person-centred residential aged care service providing comprehensive care for older people. Led by a dedicated, highly skilled, and values-driven leadership team, the facility delivers individualised care that supports wellbeing, dignity, and quality of life, aligned with each resident's personal care goals.

With a strong focus on partnership in care, residents are supported to remain active participants in decision-making, ensuring their needs, choices, and preferences are always respected.

Working at Hammill House, you'll join a professional and supportive team committed to excellence, transparency, and a positive workplace culture. The facility provides 24-7 onsite Registered Nurse coverage and actively supports ongoing professional development. You'll contribute to an environment built on respect, dignity, and meaningful connection, while being encouraged to share feedback, support innovation, and participate in continuous improvement.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Temporary
Remuneration: Public Hospital Medical Officers (State) Award
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM30169

Paediatric Basic Trainee

NSW Paediatric Physician Training Networks (Western, Northern, Eastern)

Paediatric Basic Training positions are accredited for basic training in General Paediatrics or Subspecialty training as outlined by the Royal Australasian College of Physicians. These positions are attached to one of the NSW Paediatric Physician Training Networks (i.e. Western, Northern, or Eastern), each which is made up of a number of health care facilities. As these are network positions, they involve training in a variety of locations and clinical departments. Duties will be performed at more than one place of work. To comply with Royal Australasian College of Physicians (RACP) training program requirements, trainees may be required to work in accredited facilities (including private hospitals). Facilities may be outside of NSW. The composition of each training network is provided in the attached document. There may be additional accredited facilities not listed. 

This position is open to all applicants and is also targeted for Aboriginal and - or Torres Strait Islander people. Aboriginal and - or Torres Strait Islander people are encouraged to apply and greater consideration will be given to suitable Aboriginal - Torres Strait Islander applicants, in order to improve access to employment and career opportunities. Exemption is claimed under Section 21 of the Anti-Discrimination Act 1977, NSW. If applying as an Australian Aboriginal- Torres Strait Islander, please include some information about your Aboriginal Australian - Torres Strait Islander identity in the cover letter of your application. If offered an interview, you can expand on this information at the interview itself in response to questions.

Begin Your Journey as an Orderly at Eyre and Far North Local Health Network!

Transporting pathology and other specimens in line with handling protocols

About our Role

Senior Resident Medical Officer (SRMO) positions in the Eastern & Greater Southern Surgical Skills Training Network - Prince of Wales Hospital (EGSSSTN - POWH) are designed for Junior Medical Officers who are pursuing a career in surgery. These roles provide the opportunity to deliver effective surgical care to patients under supervision in complex clinical environments while supporting preparation for a future surgical career.

SRMOs are expected to develop advanced clinical capability, including the ability to supervise more junior medical officers and, at times, undertake responsibilities aligned with accredited surgical trainees. This may include the assessment and initial management of emergency surgical patients referred for consultations.

SRMOs provide high-quality clinical management of surgical patients across EGSSTN - POWH. Your base hospital will be Prince of Wales Hospital, with rotations across a diverse range of metropolitan and regional network sites. Rotations may include:

Prince of Wales Hospital

General Surgery - including Acute Surgical Unit

Cardiothoracic Surgery

Vascular Surgery

Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery

Surgical Close Observation Unit

Upper GI-Gen Surgery (to be confirmed)

Metropolitan Hospitals

Hand Unit (Sydney and Sydney Eye Hospital)

Rural-Regional Hospitals

General Surgery (Dubbo Base Hospital)

General Surgery (Griffith Base Hospital)

General Surgery (Bega - South East Regional Hospital)

You will work as a key member of the multidisciplinary team, managing surgical patients and dealing with urgent or sensitive clinical matters with professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality. Clinical decision-making and supervision will be aligned with your level of experience, with increasing independence in patient management expected over time under the guidance of the supervising Attending Medical Officer (AMO). All patients remain under the care of a specialist, and all clinical decisions must be clearly communicated with the responsible consultant.

For further information, please refer to our website: Eastern & Greater Southern Surgical Skills Training Network - POWH (EGSSSTN - POWH)

In the remote communities of Cleve, Cowell, and Kimba, a Community Support Worker does more than complete a checklist - you help someone stay in the home they love, on their own terms. Your Role in the Community

Performing household tasks including cleaning, laundry, meal preparation, and minor gardening

 Apply now
 Job no: 944342

 Work type: Full time

 Categories: Community and Social Services, Child, Aged and Disability Care, Nursing-Midwifery





 

Yorke and Northern Local Health Network, Riverton Hospital

Registered and Enrolled Nurses

Salary: $77,824 to $106,187 p.a. (pro rata) RN-M1 | $66,552 - $77,824 p.a. (pro rata) ENC-END

Eligibility Open to Everyone 

Riverton Hospital - where care feels personal and careers feel meaningful

Registered Nurse 

Permanent 3.33FTE

Enrolled Nurse

Permanent 0.84FTE

WHERE YOU'LL BE AND WHAT YOU'LL DO

Riverton Hospital has 7 acute beds and 17 RAC aged care beds. We are a small, yet dynamic hospital servicing the local town and surrounding communities. Linked onsite with the local GP clinic, you will be exposed to a variety of patient presentations from emergency retrieval, low priority attendances, palliation, long term aged care, and everything in between - there is something for everyone at Riverton Hospital!

Set in the beautiful country town of Riverton, South Australia, 89km from Adelaide CBD. As a nurse you will fulfill a role that is engaging, fulfilling and a valued part of the country community.

Riverton is a friendly, peaceful, and scenically beautiful town, nested in the rolling hills just north of Roseworthy and not far from the renowned Clare Valley. With local schools, shops, and services there is everything you might need on hand, and if not, it's not a far drive to other nearby centres.

Our hospital and aged care facility thrive on a positive culture, where staff are valued and recognised as significant contributors to the ongoing health and wellbeing of the community we care for. We value everyone's skills, experience and contribution and emphasise a positive mindset aiming to bring our best to our work every day. You will be part of a team that works together, to support each other and provide the best service we can for our patients and our residents. We are proud of our facility and proud to be a part of the community of Riverton - come and join us!

Role Overview

Your role as a nurse will be varied, exciting, and full of opportunity! Given we are a country hospital, our nurses are known for being able to manage whatever comes through our doors, whether it is a critical event or a low priority attendance. You will develop and maintain your skills in triage, acute emergency, mental health, palliation and so much more. In addition, our attached residential aged care facility will offer you a solid nursing foundation in the ongoing management of the care of our valued residents and the challenges and accomplishment that working in aged care can bring.

There will also be opportunity to take on additional portfolios such as blood management, palliative care, education of students, work health and safety, infection control and many others. We offer extensive education opportunities to all our nursing staff as well as opportunities for career advancement into specialist acute roles, education, management, and others. Wherever you want to head with your nursing career, we can help you get there in the Yorke and Northern Local Health Network.

WHO ARE WE AND WHAT WE OFFER?

The Yorke and Northern Local Health Network (YNLHN) supports and fosters a culture in which employees feel they belong and feel safe in their work environment encouraging all people to use their talents and be valued and rewarded for their contributions.

A career in the YNLHN can be very rewarding and comes with great lifestyles benefits. Not to mention your choice of scenery from farm to ocean, vineyards, and the Southern Flinders Ranges.

Teaching and mentorship

Research opportunities

Ultrasound training

Trauma care

Dedicated education terms

Both Unaccredited and ACEM Trainees benefit from diverse clinical environments designed to support professional growth and development.

As an Unaccredited Trainee in Emergency Medicine, your primary role is to deliver high-quality medical care to undifferentiated patients presenting to the Emergency Department, under appropriate supervision.

Our Emergency Medicine Network is fully accredited by the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM) and meets all training requirements. Robust weekly education sessions.

A highly regarded Simulation Centre with innovative training sessions led by dedicated FACEMs

Opportunities to complete the Emergency Medicine Certificate (6 months), Diploma (12 months), or the Advanced Diploma (18 months).

Our district's Hospital Skills Program and Work-Based Assessment Program, designed to support professional development at every level

Communicating assessment and management plans with patients, families, and the broader healthcare team

Coordinating diagnostic investigations and specialist consultations

Managing the discharge process, including liaising with local GPs and community care providers to ensure safe, effective post-discharge care

This position also meets the ED placement requirement for selection into the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM) training program and the Training Stage 1 requirements of the ACEM training program.

We are seeking high calibre, experienced and collaborative Critical Care Specialists for VMO roles in our Northern Retrieval Advice and Coordination Service (NRACS).
 

About the Role
As a VMO with NRACS, you will participate in a cooperative 24-7 roster, providing expert critical care consultation, retrieval advice and patient transfer coordination. You will be available throughout your rostered shift to support clinicians managing critically ill and injured patients, ensuring advice and communication are delivered with professionalism, compassion and a patient-centred approach.

Working collaboratively with NSW Ambulance, Hunter Retrieval Service and Tamworth Retrieval Service and other retrieval service providers, intensive care units, emergency departments and specialty networks, you will support the timely assessment, stabilisation and transport planning of patients requiring higher levels of care. The role contributes to high-quality patient outcomes through clinical expertise, effective communication, coordination and system-wide collaboration.
 

In addition, you will contribute to clinical governance, quality improvement initiatives and service development activities that support excellence in critical care advice and coordination across the region.
 

Key Responsibilities
- Provide expert critical care advice regarding patient assessment, resuscitation, stabilisation and inter-hospital transport planning.
- Coordinate patient transfer priorities for critically ill and injured patients in collaboration with Hunter Retrieval Service and Tamworth Retrieval Service and NSW Ambulance.
- Provide critical care and logistical advice to the Newcastle and Tamworth medical retrieval teams for both pre-hospital and inter-hospital missions.
- Liaise effectively with ICUs, emergency departments, retrieval services, specialty networks and patient flow units across the health system.
- Maintain oversight of critical care bed availability and contribute to system-wide decision-making during periods of high demand or major clinical events.
- Participate in multidisciplinary reviews, debriefs, clinical audits, research activities and quality improvement initiatives.
- Provide mentorship, support and education to ical staff, retrieval coordinators and nursing personnel.
- Represent the service in relevant clinical and operational forums.
- Promote a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, safety and excellence in patient-centred care.
 

About You
You are an experienced critical care specialist with excellent clinical judgement, strong communication skills and the ability to make sound decisions in complex and time-critical situations. You thrive in collaborative environments and are committed to supporting clinicians, patients and health services through expert advice, coordination and clinical leadership.

Essential Requirements
- Primary medical degree registrable with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA).
- Fellowship of the: 
 o Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM); or
 o College of Intensive Care Medicine of Australia and New Zealand (CICM); or
 o Australian and New Zealand College of Anaesthetists (ANZCA).
- Significant current experience in emergency medicine, intensive care medicine, anaesthesia and retrieval medicine.
- Demonstrated expertise in the stabilisation and management of critically ill patients.
- Experience in leadership, coordination or decision-making roles within complex clinical systems.
- Exceptional communication, collaboration and telehealth consultation skills.
- Strong and current understanding of NSW Health retrieval systems, critical care networks and patient flow processes.
- Previous pre-hospital medical experience is highly desirable.

NRACS plays a critical role in supporting access to specialist care across Hunter New England and surrounding regions. Looking for more than just a job? Come and experience the lifestyle and professional growth Newcastle and its surrounding areas have to offer. From the breathtaking coastlines and lively local scenes to the welcoming rural charm of Tamworth, these areas combine relaxation and activity in perfect balance. Teaching and mentorship

Research opportunities

Ultrasound training

Trauma care

Dedicated education terms

As you progress from an Unaccredited Trainee to an ACEM Trainee, you'll be supported every step of the way. Our goal is to help shape not only exceptional emergency physicians but also well-rounded individuals who value and contribute to our local community.

You will be working across our dynamic Emergency Medicine Network, which include our key sites: John Hunter Hospital, The Maitland Hospital, Calvary Mater Newcastle, Belmont District Hospital, Tamworth Rural Referral Hospital, and Port Macquarie Base Hospital. These sites provide an exceptional mix of metropolitan and rural experiences, offering broad exposure to Emergency Medicine and a variety of specialities. Both Unaccredited and ACEM Trainees benefit from diverse clinical environments designed to support professional growth and development.

What you'll be doing

As an Unaccredited Trainee in Emergency Medicine, your primary role is to deliver high-quality medical care to undifferentiated patients presenting to the Emergency Department, under appropriate supervision.

Our Emergency Medicine Network is fully accredited by the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM) and meets all training requirements. We are proud to support our trainees with outstanding education, exam preparation, and clinical experience. Our current exam success rates reflect the strength of our program.

We are proud to report outstanding recent success rates in the AMC Clinical (Part 2) Examination.

Robust weekly education sessions.

Opportunities to complete the Emergency Medicine Certificate (6 months), Diploma (12 months), or the Advanced Diploma (18 months).

Our district's Hospital Skills Program and Work-Based Assessment Program, designed to support professional development at every level

Communicating assessment and management plans with patients, families, and the broader healthcare team

Managing the discharge process, including liaising with local GPs and community care providers to ensure safe, effective post-discharge care

This position also meets the ED placement requirement for selection into the Australasian College for Emergency Medicine (ACEM) training program and the Training Stage 1 requirements of the ACEM training program.

At the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, every role helps children and young people live their healthiest lives.

As the largest paediatric health service in Australia, we care for thousands of children each year, in hospital and at home. Our people are united by compassion, collaboration and excellence in care.

Sydney Children's Hospital (SCH), Randwick, one of Australia's leading specialist centres for children, has entered an exciting new chapter with the opening of the Bilima Building in November 2025.

This state-of-the-art redevelopment enhances our ability to deliver world-class care to seriously ill and injured children from across NSW and beyond. 

We are seeking nurses to join our 18-bed tertiary Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU), caring for critically ill infants, children and young people requiring highly specialised and complex care, supported by a skilled multidisciplinary team. We are committed to supporting your success in this challenging and rewarding specialty. You will be welcomed into a strong, approachable leadership team and benefit from structured education, dedicated preceptorship and supported clinical development. For nurses new to the PICU environment, we offer a tailored Specialist Transition Program (STP), designed to build your confidence, knowledge and clinical capability in intensive care nursing. 

As part of the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, SCH provides a comprehensive range of paediatric and adolescent medical and surgical services, caring for children with a wide variety of complex conditions. Located in Sydney's eastern suburbs and co-located with Prince of Wales Hospital and the Royal Hospital for Women, our campus offers easy access to beaches, amenities and public transport. 

You'll be part of a warm, supportive culture focused on excellence in care and improving outcomes for children and their families.

To be eligible to apply for this position, applicants must hold a valid visa with unrestricted working rights in Australia, or be an Australian citizen or permanent resident.
